real_defects.issue: Carried-over (disallowed) wash-sale loss was stored as share/rep.qty per share on the whole purchase and charged on every share later sold from it, so a 100-share replacement buy that absorbed a 30-share wash added the $300 loss 100/30 times ($1,000) to the later sale's basis, overstating the Form 8949 loss by $700; two washes into one buy also summed their per-share amounts over different share counts. Fixed: each wash pushes {qty, perShare} onto the buy's carried list, consumed first and only for those shares; adjustedBasisPerShare is per wash. Tests: three new cases in calc.test.mjs.

A later loss sale could designate shares that already carried an earlier wash loss as its own replacement shares (taxable avail used b.free, which never shrinks when designated shares are sold), so the same held shares carried two losses and the next sale's basis was overstated (random trial 2: reported -1731.31 vs real -2525 over a closed position). Fixed: a taxable buy's available replacement shares = qty - soldFromTaxable - shares still carrying a wash loss. Test: 'shares already carrying a wash loss are not replacement shares for a second loss sale', plus the 300-trial basis-conservation property that found it.
